# Verify the numbers, then prove the method

Most pages in this category are **mathematical recall cards**, not code tutorials. This small Python file checks representative numbers after you have understood the underlying proof.

Run from the repository root:

~~~bash
python3 interviews/tips-and-notes/algorithm-math/examples/algorithm_math_lab.py
python3 -m unittest discover -s interviews/tips-and-notes/algorithm-math/examples -p 'test_*.py'
~~~

It checks prefix sums, subarray counting (including negative numbers), fixed windows, difference arrays, binary-search thresholds, DP, knapsack, LIS, maximum subarray sum, an unweighted shortest path, greedy intervals, arithmetic identities and polynomial hash examples.

The entire lab is standard-library Python and is intentionally **not** a collection of complete LeetCode solutions. A passing test validates numerical examples; it cannot by itself establish the correctness of a technique on every input.
